core: 需要 expresses a genuine requirement for an item, action, or help. Learners often overuse it for polite offers, where 要不要 sounds much more natural in everyday speech.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ xū yào hē diǎn shén me ma?
sentences.en: Would you like something to drink?
sentences.why: A friend or family member asks what you want to drink before or during a visit. It is a warm, caring check-in rather than a strict requirement.
sentences.tip: If you are offering something, 要不要 is even more common in casual speech than 需要.

sentences.situation: At a convenience store · cashier to customer
sentences.why: Cashiers in China ask this standard question to decide whether to give you a plastic bag. It is short, practical, and repeated every day in shops.
sentences.tip: A quick answer is 要 or 不用了.

sentences.situation: With a close friend · offering help
sentences.pinyin: Nǐ xū yào bāng máng jiù gào sù wǒ.
sentences.en: Tell me if you need help.
sentences.why: You say this to someone moving house, fixing something, or dealing with a problem. It means you are willing to help, but you do not push.
sentences.tip: Said with a soft, calm tone; it sounds caring, not like an order.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ jīn tiān xū yào chuān wài tào.
sentences.en: You need to wear a jacket today.
sentences.why: A parent tells a child this when it is cold outside. It is a gentle requirement, not a suggestion, because the parent is responsible for the child.
sentences.tip: For a friend, 最好穿件外套 sounds softer and less parental.

sentences.situation: In a WeChat message · colleague to colleague
sentences.pinyin: Zhè ge bào gào míng tiān xū yào jiāo.
sentences.en: This report needs to be handed in tomorrow.
sentences.why: A colleague reminds another person of a deadline. It is clear and practical, without blaming anyone.
sentences.tip: The word 交 is common for turning in homework or work documents.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ men xū yào tí qián zhǔn bèi.
sentences.en: We need to prepare in advance.
sentences.why: A manager says this before a meeting, event, or client visit. It means the group must start early, not wait until the last minute.
sentences.tip: 提前 means ahead of time; it is a very common workplace word.

sentences.situation: At a restaurant · waiter to customer
sentences.pinyin: Nín hái xū yào diǎn bié de ma?
sentences.en: Would you like to order anything else?
sentences.why: A waiter uses 您 to show respect and asks whether the customer wants more food or drink. It is a standard polite check-in during a meal.
sentences.tip: If you are full, say 不用了，谢谢.

sentences.pinyin: Nǐ xū yào hǎo hǎo xiū xi yī xià.
sentences.en: You need to get some good rest.
sentences.why: You say this to someone who looks exhausted after work, travel, or illness. It is a kind suggestion based on real concern.
sentences.tip: 好好 means properly or well; it makes the advice sound warm.

sentences.zh: 这个项目需要更多时间。
sentences.pinyin: Zhè ge xiàng mù xū yào gèng duō shí jiān.
sentences.why: A client or project manager explains why a task cannot be finished quickly. It states a practical need, not an excuse.
sentences.tip: 项目 is a common word for project in business settings.

sentences.pinyin: Xiè xiè, wǒ bù xū yào le.
sentences.why: You use this when a shop assistant, cashier, or friend offers something you do not want. It is polite because you say 谢谢 first, then make a clear refusal.
sentences.tip: Do not say just 不需要; it can sound cold. Always add 谢谢.

quiz.prompt: A shop cashier asks if you need a bag. You do not need one. Say it politely.
quiz.explain: Starting with 谢谢 makes the refusal polite in Chinese service situations.

quiz.prompt: You are a café worker asking a customer if they need something to drink.
quiz.explain: Using 您 is polite for customers; the question is short and natural.

quiz.prompt: Your boss says the team is rushing too much before a meeting. Tell them calmly that you need to prepare in advance.
quiz.answer: 我们需要提前准备一下。
quiz.explain: 提前准备 is the natural workplace phrase for preparing ahead of time.

quiz.prompt: A friend looks very tired after a long week. Gently tell them they need to rest well.
quiz.explain: 好好休息 sounds caring and is commonly used when someone is tired.

quiz.prompt: 服务员问你：“您还需要点别的吗？” 你已经吃饱了，礼貌地回答。
quiz.answer: 不用了，谢谢，我不需要了。
quiz.explain: 不用了，谢谢 is the standard polite way to decline extra food or drink.

quiz.prompt: 同事说这个报告今天就要交，但你觉得时间不够。你怎么自然地说明情况？
quiz.answer: 这个报告今天交有点紧，我需要更多时间。
accept: 今天可能交不完，我需要更多时间。
时间有点紧，我需要再准备一下。
quiz.explain: This explains the practical need for more time without sounding rude.
